title: Stacked Generalization
source_result: Original journal-paper scan (mirror, not secondary discussion). Level-1 data come from predictions of level-0 generalizers on excluded examples; a generalizer is learned in the space of these guesses. No restriction to a common convex mixture. Footnote explicitly says another scheme or a single generalizer can outperform stacking.
project_inference: Separate general stacked prediction from hard expert routing; exclude in-sample meta-training optimism.
known_limits: Finite data, choice of level-1 representation/model, excluded-instance behavior versus final fit. No universal accuracy improvement.
verification_status: original journal scan on mirror opened; cited sections verified

title: Stacked Regressions
source_result: Uses cross-validated level-one predictions; nonnegative least squares weights. Under additional sum-one constraint squared residual risk is alpha^T R alpha. Best single predictor k is optimal among convex averages iff R_kk <= R_ik for all i. Paper itself says general empirical-improvement proof not in place.
project_inference: Residual dependence, not expert count alone, determines squared-error complementarity; do not transfer regression theorem to Top1.
known_limits: Theorem is fixed squared-error residual geometry, not multiclass Top1, not dynamic-gate generalization. Regression implementation does not generally require sum weights = 1; do not confuse nonnegative weights with convex weights.
verification_status: primary full text opened; cited sections verified

title: Issues in Stacked Generalization
authors: Kai Ming Ting; Ian H. Witten
source_result: Level-one inputs full class-probability vectors compared with hard classes. Their multiclass linear regressor uses class-specific coefficients LR_l=sum_k alpha_kl P_kl; not one common simplex of expert weights. Probability/MLR wins over BestCV on nine of ten datasets and ties on one in reported comparison.
project_inference: Read complete expert opinions; class-specific stacking lies beyond common convex-expert weights.
known_limits: Specific datasets/learners and cross-validation design; not guarantee for frozen neural solver selectors; learned outputs are scores, not automatically calibrated probabilities.
verification_status: primary full text opened; cited sections verified

title: META-DES: A Dynamic Ensemble Selection Framework using Meta-Learning
authors: Rafael M. O. Cruz; Robert Sabourin; George D. C. Cavalcanti; Tsang Ing Ren
source_result: Meta-target is per-classifier correctness. Meta-inputs include neighbors hard correctness, posterior probability, overall local accuracy, correctness on similar output profiles, and query classifier confidence. Generalization extracts features using labeled DSEL and output profiles then selects competent classifiers and combines decisions.
project_inference: Opinion profiles and legal TRAIN context can inform conditional competence without accessing query truth.
known_limits: Pool expansion produces correlated meta-examples, not independent samples; local competence may not transfer; hard voting cannot choose class nobody votes for; its sample-selection thresholds are NOT recommendations here. Project context must use TRAIN only with query/base exclusion.
verification_status: primary full text opened; cited sections verified

title: Bayesian hierarchical stacking: Some models are (somewhere) useful
authors: Yuling Yao; Gregor Pirs; Aki Vehtari; Andrew Gelman
read_sections: Sections 2.3-2.4 Eqs.11-14; Section 3.2 Theorems 1-4, Eqs.19 and 23
source_result: Input-varying partially pooled predictive mixture weights maximize a log predictive score using out-of-sample densities; hierarchy models weight uncertainty. Theorem 3 bounds population log-score gain under local separation. Theorem 4 for pointwise selection versus global stacking additionally assumes strong separation and EXACTLY KNOWN input regions I_k. Theorem 1 approximates objective value at weights Pr(J_k), not generic equivalence of weight and correctness probability.
project_inference: Conditional predictive mixture is a distinct statistical object; local diversity only helps when its conditioning structure is learnable.
known_limits: Oracle expressiveness/log-score statements are not learnability or finite-sample Top1 guarantees. Model index differs from solver-action index; nonzero winning region need not imply positive weight without conditions. Do not claim nonzero true-winner frequency forces nonzero argmax selection.
verification_status: primary full text opened; cited sections verified

title: Combining Predictive Distributions
source_result: For distinct component forecasts, fixed strictly positive weights, regularity and neutral dispersion, Theorem 3.1(c) says linear pool overdispersed. Theorem 3.2: fixed positive linear combination formula incoherent in the specified distribution class; coherence is aggregation-as-conditional-law notion.
project_inference: Do not assume an average of individually calibrated forecasts is calibrated; no universal negative claim about conditional multiclass pooling.
known_limits: Not a theorem that every input-dependent multiclass gate is uncalibrated or that linear pooling cannot improve accuracy. Use to reject automatic preservation of calibration. Do not suggest beta/temperature grids.
verification_status: primary full text opened; cited sections verified

title: Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
source_result: Expected score uniquely optimized by truth in unrestricted predictive-distribution space. Strict proper scoring concerns forecasting target distribution, not a guarantee every empirical score improvement changes downstream decisions.
project_inference: Specify which event is forecast: expert correctness versus native winner; proper score improvements need not change hard decisions.
known_limits: Only introduction definition extracted reliably; later targeted web fetch timed out. Do not claim later theorem or section read. Need distinguish binary correctness probability from categorical native-winner probability.

title: Composite Multiclass Losses
authors: Robert C. Williamson; Elodie Vernet; Mark D. Reid
source_result: Continuous multiclass loss strictly proper iff c-calibrated for every interior c. At uniform c, strictly proper continuous loss yields Fisher-consistent argmax classification; proper loss controls statistical target and link parametrizes computation.
project_inference: Separate proper winner probability estimation from finite-class convex-hull approximation and continuous decision cost.
known_limits: Population/unrestricted conditional prediction, not finite-sample neural optimization or misspecified convex hull. Does not recover sample-specific continuous cost magnitudes from winner labels.
verification_status: primary full text opened; cited sections verified

title: Multiclass Classification, Information, Divergence, and Surrogate Risk
authors: John Duchi; Khashayar Khosravi; Feng Ruan
read_sections: Section 3.2 Definition 3.1 Eq.13; Sections 4.1-4.3 Definition 4.1, Theorems 1-2, Lemma 4.1
source_result: Cost-matrix calibration is distinct from zero-one calibration. For jointly choosing representation/quantizer and discriminant, universal equivalence is stronger: Theorem 1 affine relation of generalized entropies iff same ordering all priors. Learned compression cannot be certified by fixed-representation Fisher consistency alone.
project_inference: Do not infer decision-optimal representations from fixed-representation calibration; fixed class-cost matrix is not an instance-cost vector.
known_limits: Fixed class-dependent cost matrices do not encode instance-dependent full routing-cost vectors. Quantizer/population and estimation/approximation assumptions do not prove this architecture fails or succeeds.
verification_status: primary full text opened; cited sections verified

title: Smart Predict, then Optimize
read_sections: Section 3.2 Definition 3.5 and Proposition 3.6; Section 4 Assumption 4 and Theorem 4.2
source_result: SPO measures realized cost of prediction-induced decision minus oracle. SPO+ upper bounds SPO and is convex in predicted cost. Theorem 4.2 consistency assumes unique conditional-mean optimum, centrally symmetric conditional costs, continuous density on whole R^d, nonempty interior feasible region.
project_inference: Use full TRAIN action losses to define regret-aware decisions; retain separate native-winner objective and theorem assumptions.
known_limits: Finite action selection is inner argmin over methods, not new route optimization. Full simplex has empty interior in ambient space, costs/regret have special constrained support and single stored realizations; cannot simply quote theorem. Actual regret uses per-instance normalization before conditional expectation, not ratio of means; proper CE targets native winner separately.
verification_status: primary full text opened; cited sections verified
